title: Docs architecture: a readable README, focused documents, one link map
description:
Operator directive, 2026-08-19. The README is 149KB and the adoption goal is failed by a document nobody can read alone: reduce it to a brief value proposition with the testimonials, the quick start for end users, and links out to focused documents, with everything else split into smaller focused documentation. Pairs with ifd.117 (the 118KB configuration guide split) as one effort with one structure decision.

Role split, confirmed by the product manager: the product manager owns what the README is for and drafts the new opening structure, with the operator's approval on the result; developers execute the split across runs with reconciled docs as definition of done; reviewers enforce truth; the architect has a voice on anchor stability and cross-link structure, and the structure child states the moved-anchor policy up front rather than each run discovering it. A technical-writer persona was considered and deferred: review already enforces writing quality adversarially, and a new role is a harness change worth making only if documentation structure still lacks an owner after this restructure.

Ordering, per the product manager: the structure decision spans both documents so the link map lands once; the adoption walkthrough's asserted claims must stay true through the split, and that test gates the merges, not review alone.

Done means a newcomer can read the README start to finish, reach a working first run from its quick start, and find everything else one link away; no anchor cited by an item or design dangles.
notes:
Admitted to the backlog by the product manager in conversation chat-91253e0e070c17b0663651cc48602122, after turn 126.

Reason: Approved by the operator twice while the proposal seam was broken; re-admitted as proposed now that admission is goal-level per ifd.25's design. The adoption goal enforced on its primary surface. Children and the ifd.117 reparent follow once this id exists.

Goal served: A newcomer can go from the documented install to a working first run on their own repository using the readme alone.

Review summary: The split itself is careful and mostly well executed: the README keeps its value proposition, install, and three-step quick start and now ends in a Further reading map that reaches all six new documents plus the configuration guide, design, Slack setup, and docs/product; every relative link and fragment I could resolve in the visible patch resolves correctly (including the reparented ones like designs/v1-harness-design.md#what-is-enforced-and-what-is-not, ../scripts/yoyo-status-test.sh, and ../README.md#further-reading); docs/configuration.md's cross-reference to the role table was repointed at conversation.md; internal/contextbundle was widened to carry the six new operator documents and the README and conversation.md were both updated to describe that widening consistently, with test coverage added; and docs/docs-map.md was reconciled rather than left asserting the old sizes and citation tables. The docs-map edit also discloses, rather than hides, that this run landed the document list early against the rule that document states, and says an amendment was raised to settle it — I cannot verify that amendment from my evidence, but docs/docs-map.md is not one of the artifact homes a protected-path grant governs, so I am not treating the edit itself as a boundary violation. Neither delivered invariant is touched: nothing here acquires or releases a promotion lease or performs a promotion, and nothing changes how work is selected or why that selection is recorded; the prose describing both was moved intact. Two things hold approval back: the split orphaned the /diff and /redirect explanations from the document that lists them, and the evidence contains no run of the two verifications this effort's definition of done rests on. Bounds worth stating: the patch is truncated, so docs/work.md, the second half of docs/reporting.md, scripts/check-doc-links.py, and all three Go files' actual hunks were not shown to me and are unreviewed rather than approved — in particular I could not confirm that docs/work.md carries the #letting-the-harness-choose-the-work and #reviewing-what-a-branch-adds-up-to anchors the README and docs/operations.md now link into.
Finding [major] (docs/reporting.md:0): The split moved the `/diff` and `/redirect` explanations into docs/reporting.md but left both commands listed only in docs/conversation.md, with no link between the two. A reader in conversation.md sees `/diff [id]` and `/redirect <id> <what to do differently>` in the command table, gets no explanation of either, and is pointed nowhere; worse, the Directives section now opens "A redirection is about one item. A directive is about the product" with its antecedent in a different file. That is the findability the item's done criterion is about ("find everything else one link away"), and reporting.md's own subtitle — "For an operator asking what the work cost and what came back" — does not describe /redirect, which is steering. Move the `/redirect` paragraph back into conversation.md's "Steering the work from the conversation" section immediately before "Directives, and the work they pause" so the contrast has its antecedent again, and either move `/diff` with it or add an explicit link from conversation.md to reporting.md#what-the-work-cost for it.
Finding [major] (docs/developing-yoyo.md:0): Nothing in the evidence exercises the two verifications this change's correctness rests on. The check results are make fmtcheck/test/race/vet, none of which resolves a Markdown link or walks the quick start, while the work item states that the adoption walkthrough's claims "must stay true through the split, and that test gates the merges, not review alone", and docs/developing-yoyo.md (added here) tells readers that a change touching what they cover should run `scripts/check-doc-links.py` and `scripts/walk-adoption.sh`. This change moves 22 README sections and rewrites the citations of them across Markdown and Go source, which is exactly the failure yoyodyne-ifd.54 already hit once with dead anchors that no reviewer caught. Run both scripts against this tree and report their output with the change; if `scripts/walk-adoption.sh` does not exist at that path, docs/developing-yoyo.md is asserting a script that is not there and needs correcting instead.
